_about: Documented patches applied to the upstream historical-basemaps GeoJSON before processing. Every entry must carry a 'note' (what & why) and a 'source' (citation for the correct fact). Entries match features by exact raw NAME string (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized) in one snapshot year (signed; negative = BC), or in every snapshot within an inclusive 'from'/'to' range. 'set' rewrites properties; 'drop': true removes the feature. Ambiguous cases are NOT patched here — they are disclosed in ERRATA.md instead.

corrections.note: The 1500 BC snapshot labels the Chinese heartland (bbox ~104–122E, 27–40N) 'Zhoa'. Around 1500 BC the polity dominating the Yellow River heartland is the Shang state (c. 1600–1046 BC); 'Zhoa' appears to be a garbled 'Zhou', a dynasty that had not yet risen.
corrections.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Shang dynasty'; Cambridge History of Ancient China (1999), ch. 3

corrections.note: The 1930 snapshot labels the entire Soviet Union (bbox spanning -180..180E, 35–78N) 'White Russia'. The USSR was established in December 1922 and the White movement was defeated by 1923; the sibling 1920 snapshot correctly labels the union-wide polity 'USSR' and uses 'White Russia' for the Belarus region.

The 700 AD snapshot still labels China "Sui Empire". The Sui fell in 618; in 700 China was ruled by the Tang (618–907), then under Empress Wu Zetian. The label appears carried over from the 600 AD snapshot.

The 700 AD snapshot still carries a 2.8M km² "Sasanian Empire". The Sasanian state was destroyed by the Arab conquest (Nahavand 642; last king Yazdegerd III killed 651); by 700 Iran was governed by the Umayyad Caliphate. The label appears carried over from the 600 AD snapshot.
Same stale-label case as the 700 AD Sasanian Empire: these dependencies had passed to the caliphate half a century earlier.
In 700 the Hejaz (Mecca and Medina) was the religious heartland of the Umayyad Caliphate, not a separate polity.

The 1492–1880 snapshots label eastern New Guinea with the name of a state that only came into being in 1975; the island's societies were stateless and no colonial administration existed before the 1884 German and British annexations. Relabelled to the dataset's own cultural-zone name so the polygon renders as a cultural area instead of counting 0.42M km² of phantom state land.

The 1000 AD snapshot labels the whole of Greenland (2.1M km²) 'Denmark-Norway', a union that only formed in 1524. The Norse settlements founded c. 985 were self-governing until they accepted Norwegian sovereignty in 1261; Denmark's colonial claim dates from 1721. Relabelled as a cultural zone so the polygon no longer adds two million km² to the Danish stream. The 1400 and 1500 'Kalmar Union' labels for Greenland are kept as the dataset's reading of the crown's nominal claim.

The 1938 and 1945 snapshots label the territory 'Israel', a state proclaimed on 14 May 1948; in both years it was the British Mandate for Palestine (1920–1948). Relabelled with the mandate's name so the map does not show a state a decade before it existed.

The 1492 snapshot has no Inca polygon at all. The north Peruvian coast keeps the label 'Chimú', but the Kingdom of Chimor was conquered by the Inca under Topa Inca Yupanqui c. 1470; in 1492 it was part of the Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu). The 1400 snapshot rightly has a separate Chimú, and 1500 and 1530 already say 'Inca Empire'.
corrections.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Chimú" and "Inca" (Topa Inca Yupanqui's conquest of Chimor, c. 1470)

corrections.note: The central Peruvian highlands are labelled 'Wari' in 1492; the Wari Empire collapsed by c. 1100 and the area was the Inca heartland in 1492.

The Inca heartland of highland Peru is drawn in 1492 only as the Quechua people (0.76M km²). Every Quechua-speaking region on the polygon had been incorporated into the Inca Empire by the 1480s, so the polygon is relabelled to the state that governed it. Even so the empire remains under-drawn (about 0.9M km² against the conventional ~2M km²): Ecuador, the Bolivian altiplano and north-west Argentina are drawn as other peoples and are left as cultural zones rather than reconstructed.
corrections.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Inca" (extent under Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac)
